limits.note:
Text-to-video and image-to-video with synchronized native audio, up to 1080p. Workflow auto-detected: a prompt alone is text-to-video, adding a source image is image-to-video.

**Prompting**

- There is no separate negative prompt. To steer away from unwanted elements, describe them in your prompt, for example: "a calm forest at dawn, avoid blurry motion, no on-screen text".

**Multi-shot**

- Generate up to 6 sequential shots by formatting the prompt like this (shot durations must sum to the total duration):

```
shot 1, <seconds>, <description>; shot 2, <seconds>, <description>;
```

**Input limits**

- Prompt up to 3,072 characters. Resolution 720p or 1080p. Duration 3 to 15 seconds. Aspect ratio 16:9, 9:16, or 1:1 for text-to-video (image-to-video follows the source image).
- Image inputs: JPEG or PNG, at least 300px per side, aspect within 1:2.5 to 2.5:1, up to 50 MB.

}

limits.note:
Fugu Ultra v1.1 is an updated multi-agent conductor: each request coordinates a pool of expert models and composes their work into a single answer.

**Latency and streaming**
- Responses can take from a few seconds to a few minutes on complex prompts.
- The full answer is returned all at once when the model finishes, not token by token. Streaming is accepted, but it delivers the complete response at the end rather than streaming tokens as they generate.
- max_tokens must be at least 16. Leave generous headroom, since very small limits can truncate or empty the answer.

**Capabilities**
- Text and image input, with a 1M token context.
- Always-on reasoning with high, xhigh, and a distinct max level for the hardest problems.
- Function calling, strict JSON Schema structured output, and built-in web search that cites its sources when available (no separate fee).

**Versioning**
- Use fugu-ultra-v1-1 for v1.1. The legacy fugu-ultra id remains pinned to v1.0 for backward compatibility.

**Billing**

limits.note:
Fugu Ultra v1.0 is the original multi-agent conductor: each request coordinates a pool of expert models and composes their work into a single answer.

**Latency and streaming**
- Responses can take from a few seconds to a few minutes on complex prompts.
- The full answer is returned all at once when the model finishes, not token by token. Streaming is accepted, but it delivers the complete response at the end rather than streaming tokens as they generate.
- max_tokens must be at least 16. Leave generous headroom, since very small limits can truncate or empty the answer.

**Capabilities**
- Text and image input, with a 1M token context.
- Always-on reasoning. high is the default; xhigh and max are aliases of the same maximum effort.
- Function calling, JSON mode, and built-in web search that cites its sources when available (no separate fee).

**Compatibility**
- The legacy fugu-ultra, fugu-ultra-20260615, and sakana/fugu-ultra ids remain pinned to this version.

**Billing**
- Billed on full token usage, including the orchestration tokens the model uses internally, so even short prompts carry some cost.
- Context-tiered: requests above 272K total input tokens use the higher rate shown.

- WAV output

**Controls**

- Duration 10 to 300 seconds
- Songs are billed per generated second with a 10 second floor

**Billing**

- Charged per generated second at the catalog rate. A 10 second request that returns a 10 second song bills 10 seconds.
- A request rejected before generation is not billed.

limits.tool_usage_note:
**Per-tool billing (`usage.tool_usage`)**

When this model invokes tools inside a single request, the response carries a normalized `usage.tool_usage` map alongside the token counts. The example below shows the shape. Exact field names, units, and which tools appear can vary by tool:

```json
"usage": {
  "prompt_tokens": 123,
  "completion_tokens": 456,
  "cost_usd": 0.0042,
  "tool_usage": {"web_search": 3}
}
```

The tool counts are already factored into `cost_usd` and are surfaced so you can audit per-tool billing. The field is omitted when no billed tool was invoked.

limits.note:
Text-only. This build does not accept image or video input, unlike the base Qwen3.6 35B A3B.

**Weights**

Served from the 2-bit eschamoe W2 build published by Escha Labs (eschalabs.com) as EschaLabs/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Escha-W2 on Hugging Face, under Apache-2.0. The experts are quantized to 2 bits, mixed per projection (gate_up_proj at 2-bit and down_proj at 3-bit), the dense layers are int8, and the KV cache is FP16. Escha Labs publishes the quality comparison against an FP8 baseline of the same model: parity or better on math, graduate science, tool use and long context, about 2 percent lower on broad knowledge, and about 7 percent lower on long-horizon code generation, which is the one clear gap. See the model card for the full benchmark table and protocol.

**Behavior**

Supports streaming, function tools, structured JSON output including strict schemas, and thinking mode on by default. Set enable_thinking=false for direct answers. With thinking on, the reasoning arrives in reasoning_content and the answer in content, so read both. A low max_tokens with thinking on can be spent entirely on reasoning, so allow room for the answer.

**Caching**

Automatic prefix cache reads are billed at the cached-input rate when reported. Explicit cache controls are not supported. Cancelling a streaming request mid-generation bills only the tokens produced up to that point.

data.author: empiriolabs
data.description: Answers yes/no, choice, score and tool questions about text, JSON, images, video and audio in up to 1M tokens, and can tell when the input lacks the answer.

supported_parameters.name: long_context
supported_parameters.label: Long Context
supported_parameters.description: How a state longer than 131,072 tokens is read: fast (the default) answers in seconds, full reads every token. Shorter states are always read in full.

limits.note:
**Requests**

Send content in `state` (a string, a JSON object, or an array) and 1 to 128 questions in `questions` to `POST /v1/decisions`. Each question is answered on its own, with probabilities and a confidence value. No text is generated. The [Decisions API guide](https://docs.empiriolabs.ai/decisions) documents every question option, and its [Chat formats](https://docs.empiriolabs.ai/decisions#chat-formats) section covers requests through `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages` and Gemini `generateContent`.

**Question types**

- `noul`: yes or no, answered with the probability of yes.
- `choice`: one of 2 to 255 options, answered with the chosen option and the full distribution.
- `score`: 2 to 10 ordered levels, answered with the expected level and the distribution.
- `tool`: which of 1 to 254 function tools to call, with distributions over its enum and boolean arguments.

**Not in the `state`**

Add `"abstain": true` to a `noul`, `choice` or `score` question to let the model say the state does not contain the answer. The answer then includes `abstain`, the probability of that outcome, and the rest of the answer assumes the state does contain it.

**Limits**

- The state plus the longest question: up to 1,000,000 tokens.
- At most 512 evaluated questions per request. A tool question counts as one plus one per enum or boolean argument.
- Media: up to 16 images (20 MB each), 8 audio clips (25 MB and 10 minutes each) and 4 videos (100 MB and 10 minutes each), as public HTTPS URLs or inline base64.

**Benchmarks**

Benchmark results are in the [launch post](https://empiriolabs.ai/blog/introducing-aplomb-1).

**Billing**

Input tokens only: the state once per request, each question's own text, and each media item's tokens. Output is always zero.

limits.tool_usage_note:
**Per-tool billing (`usage.tool_usage`)**

When this model invokes built-in tools (web search, code interpreter, etc.) inside a single request, the response carries a normalized `usage.tool_usage` map alongside the token counts. The example below shows the shape, exact field names, units, and which tools appear can vary slightly per provider:

```json
"usage": {
  "prompt_tokens": 123,
  "completion_tokens": 456,
  "cost_usd": 0.0042,
  "tool_usage": {"web_search": 3, "code_interpreter": 1}
}
```

The tool counts are already factored into `cost_usd`, they are surfaced for transparency so you can audit per-tool billing. The field is omitted when no tools were invoked.

Qwen Image 3.0 combines Base and Pro image generation and editing in one model. Pro is selected by default, output starts at 2K, and aspect ratio starts in Auto. Base provides a lower-cost option for fast iteration.

**Variants**

- Choose qwen-image-3.0-pro for photorealism, dense layouts, fine multilingual typography, and complex multi-image edits.
- Choose qwen-image-3.0 for lower-cost generation and routine edits.
- Choose with model_variant. Without it, the model ids qwen-image-3.0, alibaba/qwen-image-3.0 and alibaba/qwen-image-3-0 run Base and every other id of this model runs Pro.

**Modes**

- Text to image from a prompt.
- Image editing and reference-guided generation from one to three images.
- Direct prompt extension works for generation and editing. Agent prompt extension provides deeper refinement for text-to-image requests only.

**Output and input limits**

- One to six output images per request.
- 1K, 2K, automatic, aspect-ratio presets, or an exact custom size.
- Preset and custom sizes stay between 512x512 and 2048x2048 pixels, with each selected side up to 2048 pixels and aspect ratio from 1:8 to 8:1. Automatic sizing can choose its own dimensions within the 1K or 2K output tiers.
- Input images can be JPG, JPEG, PNG, BMP, TIFF, WEBP, or GIF, up to 10 MB each.
- Prompts support up to 4,500 tokens.

**Billing**

- Base uses one output rate across 1K and 2K.
- Pro outputs up to 2.25 megapixels use the 1K rate. Larger Pro outputs use the 2K rate.
- Every reference image adds the input-image rate shown above.

**Performance**

- 1K generations are optimized for interactive iteration. Complex 2K edits can take several minutes.

**Content safety**

Generated images pass an automated content-safety check. An image flagged as explicit is not returned. Because the image is generated before the check runs, a flagged generation is still billed.

limits.tool_usage_note:
**Per-tool billing (`usage.tool_usage`)**

When this model invokes tools (web search, code interpreter, etc.) inside a single request, the response carries a normalized `usage.tool_usage` map alongside the token counts. The example below shows the shape, exact field names, units, and which tools appear can vary slightly per provider:

```json
"usage": {
  "prompt_tokens": 123,
  "completion_tokens": 456,
  "cost_usd": 0.0042,
  "tool_usage": {"web_search": 3, "code_interpreter": 1}
}
```

The tool counts are already factored into `cost_usd`, they are surfaced for transparency so you can audit per-tool billing. The field is omitted when no tools were invoked.

limits.note:
**Modes**

- Text to image
- Single or multi-image to image
- Interactive editing with coordinate or sketch markers
- Layer decomposition into a base image plus up to 16 layers

**Interactive editing**

Mark the region to change directly on the input image with a sketch, circle, or arrow, then describe it in the prompt. For exact placement, use coordinate tags on a 0 to 1000 normalized grid:

```text
Place the subject from image 1 <bbox>179 283 796 986</bbox> at the position in image 2 <bbox>118 331 933 871</bbox>.
```

**Layer decomposition**

Set layer_decomposition to true with exactly one input image to split it into a base image plus up to 16 transparent PNG layers. Every returned image carries its stacking order as z_index, and each layer also carries its position in the base image as bounding_box.absolute and bounding_box.normalized, plus a name and a description. Leave the prompt empty to let the model choose the elements, or name the elements or coordinate regions to separate. Resolution accepts 1K, 1.5K, or 2K, and matches the input image when unset.

**Prompt optimization**

- Standard (default): prioritizes prompt adherence and image quality
- Fast: reduces generation latency with slightly lower image quality

**Limits**

- One output image per request, except layer decomposition, which returns the base image plus its layers
- Up to 10 reference images, and exactly one for layer decomposition or a transparent background
- 1K, 1.5K, and 2K resolution tiers
- PNG or JPEG output, and layers are always PNG
- A transparent background needs one input image that already has an alpha channel, and PNG output
- No grouped output, streaming, or web search

**Billing**

Layer decomposition bills every returned image, the base image and each layer, at half the standard per-image rate, tiered on the pixel count of that image.

**Content safety**

Generated images pass an automated content-safety check. An image flagged as explicit is not returned. Because the image is generated before the check runs, a flagged generation is still billed.

limits.note:
Generates video from a text prompt on its own, from a source image, or from up to seven reference images that keep characters and objects consistent across the shot.

**Modes**

- Text-to-video: send a prompt with no image.
- Image-to-video: add one image and it becomes the starting frame.
- Reference-to-video: add two or more images (up to seven) to carry their subjects into a new scene. Tag them in the prompt as <IMAGE_1>, <IMAGE_2>, and so on.

**Example reference-to-video prompt**

```
<IMAGE_1> and <IMAGE_2> walking together through a neon-lit street at night.
```

The mode is detected from what you send, and can be set explicitly with the mode parameter.

**Defaults**

- 10 second duration (1 to 15 seconds supported)
- 720p output (480p, 720p, or 1080p)
- Aspect ratio follows the source image for image-to-video, otherwise 16:9

**Resolution**

1080p is available for text-to-video and image-to-video. Reference-to-video supports up to 720p.

**Controls**

Supports prompt, mode, a source image or reference images (URL or upload), duration, resolution, and aspect ratio.

**Billing**

- Charged per second of generated video at the selected resolution (higher resolutions cost more per second), plus a per-image fee for each image you supply. Text-to-video has no image fee.
- A request that fails validation or errors out before any video is produced is not billed.
- A video that is produced but then blocked by content policy is still billed. This follows xAI usage policy, which charges for the generation even when the output is blocked by the content safety check. Keep prompts and source images within the usage policy to avoid this.

limits.tool_usage_note:
**Per-tool billing (`usage.tool_usage`)**

When this model invokes tools (web search, code interpreter, etc.) inside a single request, the response carries a normalized `usage.tool_usage` map alongside the token counts. The example below shows the shape, exact field names, units, and which tools appear can vary slightly per provider:

```json
"usage": {
  "prompt_tokens": 123,
  "completion_tokens": 456,
  "cost_usd": 0.0042,
  "tool_usage": {"web_search": 3, "code_interpreter": 1}
}
```

The tool counts are already factored into `cost_usd`, they are surfaced for transparency so you can audit per-tool billing. The field is omitted when no tools were invoked.

limits.note:
**Tiers**

- Plus: highest audio quality and expressiveness, for content creation, audiobooks, dubbing, and brand voice work
- Flash: tuned for real-time interaction with lower first-packet latency, for voice assistants and live agents
- Switch with the `model_tier` parameter, or send `qwen-audio-3.0-tts-plus` or `qwen-audio-3.0-tts-flash` as the model id

**Voices**

- Over 1,000 base voices, all available on both tiers, so changing tier keeps your selected voice
- Six flagship system voices are tier specific: `longanlingxin` and `longanlufeng` on Plus, and `longanhuan_v3.6`, `longjielidou_v3.6`, `loongeva_v3.6`, `loongjohn` on Flash
- Browse the full catalog with `GET /v1/voices`, and pass any voice through `voice_id`

**Custom voices**

- Set `voice` to `custom` and pass `voice_audio_url`, an https URL to 10 to 20 seconds of clear speech from one speaker.
- WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, WEBM and FLAC are accepted, up to 15 MB. Record in a quiet room, without music or other voices.
- The voice is made for the selected `model_tier`. The response includes `voice_id` and `voice_id_expires_at`: pass the `voice_id` as `voice` or `voice_id`, with the same `model_tier`, to reuse the voice for 7 days. Only the account that created it can use it.
- Each account can hold 10 custom voices on this model at a time.
- `GET /v1/voices?model=qwen-audio-3-0-tts` lists the model's voices, including your custom voices with their ids. Add `type=custom` to list custom voices alone.
- `DELETE /v1/voices/{voice_id}?model=qwen-audio-3-0-tts` deletes a custom voice, which frees its place at once.
- In the Playground, set Voice to Custom to use a saved voice again, copy its id, or delete it.
- Creating, listing and deleting custom voices adds no charge.

**Input limits**

- Up to 20,000 characters per request
- `instruction` accepts up to 128 characters
- SSML input is not supported. Use `instruction` for delivery direction, and inline tags such as `[excited]` or `[whispers]` inside the text

**Billing**

- Billed per character of input text at the selected tier's rate

limits.note:
MiniMax H3 generates 4 to 15 second clips at 24 fps in 768p or 2K, each with a native stereo audio track.

**Modes**

- Text to video: prompt only.
- Image to video: one image becomes the opening frame.
- First and last frame: supply an opening and a closing image.
- Reference to video: up to 9 images, 3 videos and 3 audio clips, 12 reference files in total.
- Regeneration: re-render a 768p clip you generated earlier at 2K. Send the original prompt plus the source clip as base_video.

**Prompt expansion**

Set `enhance_prompt` to true and the model first rewrites your brief into a full prompt, adding shot-by-shot structure, camera moves, lighting and a soundscape, then renders from that. Any reference media you attach informs the expansion. It adds a per-token charge on top of the per-second video cost, and is skipped for regeneration because that path reproduces the original request.

**Reference media**

- Images 256 to 5760 px per side, aspect ratio between 0.4 and 2.5, up to 30 MB each.
- Videos 2 to 15 seconds, H.264 or H.265, up to 50 MB each.
- Audio 2 to 15 seconds, WAV or MP3, up to 15 MB each. Reference audio requires an accompanying image or video reference.
- Reference video and audio apply to reference-to-video only.
- Prompts can be up to 7000 characters and may describe dialogue, sound effects, on-screen text, and camera work.

**Billing**

- Billed per second of the generated clip at the resolution you request.
- A reference video is billed for its own duration in addition to the generated clip, so a 5 second reference used to make a 6 second clip bills 11 seconds.
- Regeneration is billed at its own lower per-second rate, on the source clip duration plus the regenerated output. Reference images carried over from the original request are not charged again.
- The first 5 reference images are included. Each additional reference image is charged separately.
- Prompt expansion, when enabled, is billed per token.

limits.note:
Next-generation Seedance built for long-form storytelling: one request can produce a coherent clip of up to 30 seconds, draw on up to 50 reference assets, and edit or extend existing footage.

**Modes**

- Text to video, first frame, or first and last frame.
- Multimodal reference to video from up to 30 images, 10 videos, and 10 audio clips. Audio-only input works on its own.
- To edit an attached clip or continue it, describe that in your prompt. The model reads the intent from your wording.

**Output**

- 480p, 720p, and 1080p at 24fps, 4 to 30 seconds, with native synchronized audio.
- MP4 by default. MOV carries higher color precision for grading and compositing, and some players cannot open it.
- When you supply a first frame, the output follows that image's aspect ratio, so aspect_ratio stays adaptive. Reference jobs, including ones with a reference video, accept any ratio.

**Draft mode**

- Set draft to true to render a 480p draft while you are still trying shots. Drafts render at 480p only.
- The response returns the draft's id as usage.draft_task_id. Send that back as draft_task_id to render the same shot at 1080p.
- The final render takes the prompt, reference assets, duration, aspect ratio, seed and audio setting from the draft, so anything you send alongside draft_task_id is ignored. A draft stays promotable for 7 days.

**Input limits**

- Images: jpeg, png, webp, bmp, tiff, gif, heic, or heif, 300 to 6000 px per side, under 30 MB each.
- Videos: MP4 or MOV, 2 to 30 seconds each and 30 seconds in total, under 200 MB each.
- Audio: WAV or MP3, 2 to 30 seconds each and 30 seconds in total, under 15 MB each.
- Reference uploads that contain real human faces are rejected by the model. To use your own face, email support@empiriolabs.ai.

**Billing**

- Without a reference video, you are billed per second of generated video at the rate for the output resolution.
- With a reference video, the model prices the reference clip's seconds alongside the generated seconds, at the lower video-input rate. Billed seconds are therefore reference duration plus output duration, so a request that includes a reference video costs more in total than the same output generated from text alone.
- Draft mode is not a discounted rate. A draft bills as a normal 480p generation and its final bills as a normal 1080p generation, so the saving comes from trying shots at 480p and rendering only your pick at 1080p.
- Worked example at 480p: a 4 second clip from a text prompt bills 4 seconds. A 4 second clip generated from a 5 second reference video bills 9 seconds at the video-input rate.

**Uploaded media preprocessing**

- Video inputs are capped to 30 seconds.
- Uploaded video inputs are normalized to provider-compatible MP4 when needed. Set preprocess_video to false to send a clip through untouched.

limits.note:
Generates images from a text prompt, or edits up to five source images from a natural-language instruction.

**Modes**

- Text-to-image: send a prompt with no image.
- Image editing: attach one image and describe the change you want.
- Multi-image editing: attach two to five images to combine subjects, transfer a style, or compose a scene. Refer to them in the prompt as <IMAGE_0>, <IMAGE_1>, and so on.

**Example multi-image prompt**

```
Place the product from <IMAGE_0> onto the marble surface in <IMAGE_1>.
```

**Defaults**

- Auto quality at 1K resolution
- Auto aspect ratio, so the model picks the best fit for the prompt
- One output image per request

**Quality and resolution**

Quality selects how much work goes into the render. Auto lets the model choose the tier for each request and currently serves low for a text prompt and medium for an edit. Low returns in a few seconds. Medium takes longer and resolves finer detail. Resolution selects the 1K or 2K output tier. Quality and resolution combine into four price points, so a low 1K image is the cheapest option and a medium 2K image the most detailed.

**Controls**

Supports prompt, source images (URL or upload), quality, resolution, aspect ratio across sixteen ratios including auto and the 21:9 and 5:2 widescreen formats, number of images, and response format.

**Limits**

- Up to 5 source images per edit
- Up to 10 output images per request
- Prompt up to 8,000 characters

**Billing**

- Charged per output image at the quality and resolution served, plus a per-image fee for each source image you attach. Text-to-image has no source-image fee.
- With auto quality the charge follows the tier the model served for that request. Set quality to low or medium when you want the price fixed in advance.
- A request that fails validation or is rejected before any image is produced is not billed.
- An image that is produced but then blocked by content policy is still billed. This follows xAI usage policy, which charges for the generation even when the output is blocked by the content safety check. Keep prompts and source images within the usage policy to avoid this.

**Content safety**

Generated images pass an automated content-safety check. An image flagged as explicit is not returned. Because the image is generated before the check runs, a flagged generation is still billed.

limits.note:
PixVerse V6 generates video from a text prompt, a single image, a first and last frame, or up to seven reference images, and can continue an existing clip.

**Modes**

- `t2v`: text to video.
- `i2v`: animate a single image.
- `transition`: interpolate between a first-frame and a last-frame image.
- `reference`: combine up to 7 reference images, optionally with up to 3 reference videos.
- `extend`: continue an uploaded video.

**Output**

- 360p, 540p, 720p and 1080p, 1 to 15 seconds.
- Aspect ratios 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16, 2:3, 3:2 and 21:9 on text-to-video and reference modes. Image-driven modes follow the source image.
- Set `generate_audio_switch` to true for native synchronized audio.
- Set `generate_multi_clip_switch` to true on text-to-video and image-to-video for a multi-shot cut.

**Reference videos**

- Supplying `videos` in `reference` mode switches the model into omni reference. Output length is taken from the longest reference video, so `duration` is ignored.
- Name a reference with `reference_names` or `video_reference_names` and address it in the prompt as `@name` followed by a space.

**Billing**

- Billed per second of generated video at the rate for the output resolution, with a higher rate when audio is on.
- A reference request that carries a reference video bills at the video-reference rate, which is roughly double the standard rate.

**Input limits**

- Images: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 20MB and 10000px on the long edge.

limits.note:
Six transformations that take an existing video and return a new one, selected with `mode`.

**Modes**

- `modify`: edit the content of a clip from a text prompt, optionally guided by up to 3 reference images.
- `restyle`: change the visual style while preserving motion and composition. Pass a `restyle_prompt` or a `restyle_id`.
- `swap`: replace a subject in the clip with an uploaded image. The model detects the subjects in the chosen keyframe; use `swap_target` to name which one, otherwise the first detected subject is used.
- `mimic`: transfer the motion of the source video onto a subject image.
- `upscale`: raise the resolution of the clip.
- `sound_effect`: generate a synchronized sound bed. Leave the prompt empty to have it derived from the video, and set `original_sound_switch` to keep the existing audio.

**Output**

- `modify`, `mimic` and `swap` output 360p, 540p or 720p. `restyle`, `upscale` and `sound_effect` follow the source clip.

**Billing**

- Billed per second of the source video at the rate for the mode and resolution. `swap` also includes a small one-off subject-detection charge, which is folded into the billed seconds for that request.

**Input limits**

- Video: MP4, MOV or WebM, up to 1920px on the long edge and 30 seconds. Up to 100MB for modify, mimic, swap and upscale, and 50MB for restyle and sound effects. Swap requires H.264 or H.265.
- Images: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 20MB and 10000px on the long edge.

supported_parameters.label: Max Tokens
supported_parameters.description: Maximum number of output tokens for the final answer. Must be at least 32. Very small values can truncate or empty the answer. When omitted, the model's own default applies.

supported_parameters.name: reasoning_effort
supported_parameters.label: Reasoning Effort
supported_parameters.description: How hard the model reasons. Reasoning is always on. The default is high; xhigh and max are aliases of the same maximum effort.

supported_parameters.label: Web Search
supported_parameters.description: Enable built-in web search. Adds $0.007 to the request cost for each invoked call, and a single request can run more than one call. Page fetches are billed at the same rate.

supported_parameters.label: Tools
supported_parameters.description: OpenAI-compatible function calling tool definitions.

supported_parameters.name: tool_choice
supported_parameters.label: Tool Choice
supported_parameters.description: OpenAI-compatible tool choice control.

supported_parameters.name: response_format
supported_parameters.label: Structured Output
supported_parameters.description: Return structured JSON output. JSON mode returns any valid JSON object; JSON Schema mode enforces the exact schema you provide.

limits.note:
Fugu Max is the cost-efficient multi-agent conductor: each request assembles a right-sized team of expert models for the task and composes their work into a single answer.

**Latency and streaming**
- Simple prompts usually return in a few seconds, and heavier prompts take longer while the conductor works.
- The full answer is returned all at once when the model finishes, not token by token. Streaming is accepted, but it delivers the complete response at the end rather than streaming tokens as they generate.
- max_tokens must be at least 16. Leave generous headroom, since very small limits can truncate or empty the answer.

**Capabilities**
- Text and image input, with a 1M token context.
- Always-on reasoning. high is the default, xhigh raises the effort, and max is accepted as an alias of xhigh.
- Function calling, strict JSON Schema structured output, and built-in web search that cites its sources when available.

**Billing**
- Billed on full token usage, including the orchestration tokens the model uses internally, so even short prompts carry some cost.
- One flat token rate at every context length, with no higher rate for long prompts.
- Built-in web search and page fetch are billed per executed call at the rates shown, and a single request can run more than one call.
limits.tool_usage_note:
**Per-tool billing (`usage.tool_usage`)**

When this model invokes tools (web search, code interpreter, etc.) inside a single request, the response carries a normalized `usage.tool_usage` map alongside the token counts. The example below shows the shape, exact field names, units, and which tools appear can vary slightly per provider:

```json
"usage": {
  "prompt_tokens": 123,
  "completion_tokens": 456,
  "cost_usd": 0.0042,
  "tool_usage": {"web_search": 3, "code_interpreter": 1}
}
```

The tool counts are already factored into `cost_usd`, they are surfaced for transparency so you can audit per-tool billing. The field is omitted when no tools were invoked.

When this model invokes tools (web search, code interpreter, etc.) inside a single request, the response carries a normalized `usage.tool_usage` map alongside the token counts. The example below shows the shape, exact field names, units, and which tools appear can vary slightly per provider:

```json
"usage": {
  "prompt_tokens": 123,
  "completion_tokens": 456,
  "cost_usd": 0.0042,
  "tool_usage": {"web_search": 3, "code_interpreter": 1}
}
```

supported_parameters.name: instructions
supported_parameters.label: Instructions
supported_parameters.description: System guidance for how the model should behave and speak during the conversation.

supported_parameters.name: modalities
supported_parameters.label: Modalities
supported_parameters.description: Which output types the model returns for a turn. Drop audio for a text-only reply.

supported_parameters.name: input_audio_format
supported_parameters.label: Input audio format
supported_parameters.description: Encoding of the audio you append to the input buffer: base64 16-bit PCM at 16 kHz.

supported_parameters.name: output_audio_format
supported_parameters.label: Output audio format
supported_parameters.description: Encoding of the audio the model streams back: 16-bit PCM at 24 kHz.

supported_parameters.name: turn_detection
supported_parameters.label: Turn detection
supported_parameters.description: Voice activity detection: decides when you have finished speaking and the model should reply. It is on by default as server_vad, which ends your turn after a pause. semantic_vad also judges whether you have finished speaking, so filler sounds and background noise do not end your turn, and semantic_vad_ec does the same and lets you interrupt a reply more readily. threshold is a number from -1 to 1, 0.5 by default; a higher value needs clearer, louder speech to count. silence_duration_ms, from 200 to 6000 and 800 by default, is how long a pause must last to end your turn. idle_timeout_ms, from 5000 to 30000 with server_vad, makes the model speak again when you stay silent that long after its reply. Set turn_detection to null to end each turn yourself with input_audio_buffer.commit and response.create.

supported_parameters.name: max_response_output_tokens
supported_parameters.label: Max output tokens
supported_parameters.description: Largest number of output tokens one reply may use: from 1 to 65536, where a larger number runs at 65536, or "inf" for the model's own limit. Also accepted as max_output_tokens. When omitted, the model's own default applies.

supported_parameters.name: temperature
supported_parameters.label: Temperature
supported_parameters.description: Sampling temperature. 0 is deterministic and 1.99 is maximum randomness. When omitted, the model's own default applies.

supported_parameters.name: top_p
supported_parameters.label: Top P
supported_parameters.description: Nucleus sampling probability mass. Lower values make outputs more focused. When omitted, the model's own default applies.

supported_parameters.name: top_k
supported_parameters.label: Top K
supported_parameters.description: Sample only from the K most likely tokens. When omitted, the model's own default applies.

supported_parameters.name: repetition_penalty
supported_parameters.label: Repetition Penalty
supported_parameters.description: Higher values discourage repeated phrasing, and 1 applies no penalty. When omitted, the model's own default applies.

supported_parameters.name: presence_penalty
supported_parameters.label: Presence Penalty
supported_parameters.description: Penalty for tokens that already appeared in the generated text. Positive values encourage new topics. When omitted, the model's own default applies.

supported_parameters.name: seed
supported_parameters.label: Seed
supported_parameters.description: Random seed for more reproducible sampling. Reusing a seed with the same request returns similar, not always identical, output.

supported_parameters.name: video_representation_compact
supported_parameters.label: Compact video
supported_parameters.description: How the model reads the video frames you send: none keeps full detail, and normal reads the same frames for a quarter of the input tokens when fine detail is not needed. When omitted, frames keep full detail. Set it before the first audio; it cannot change after that.

limits.note:
**Connecting**

Full-duplex voice over a WebSocket at `wss://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1/realtime?model=qwen3-8-omni-flash-realtime`, authenticated with the ordinary Authorization Bearer header. Configure the session with `session.update` over the socket: voice, instructions, modalities, turn detection, sampling and the reply length limit, `max_response_output_tokens`.

**Sending audio and video**

- Append live video frames as `input_image_buffer.append` events. Frames are not message content, so an image inside a conversation item is rejected.

**Billing**

Audio and text tokens are priced separately in both directions, and each completed turn is billed on its own from the usage the model reports.

supported_parameters.name: mode

supported_parameters.description: single = one voice, multi = two-voice dialogue (uses voice + voice2 + speaker names).

supported_parameters.name: language

supported_parameters.name: voice
supported_parameters.label: Voice

limits.note:
**Limits**

- Text: up to 5,000 characters per request
- Audio billing: 32 output tokens per second of generated audio
- 130 languages. The language of the text is detected automatically.

**Voices**

- The 30 voices in the `voice` list speak every supported language.
- `GET /v1/voices?model=gemini-3-8-flash-tts` lists the full library of more than 2,000 voices across 30 locales, with the language, accent, gender, pitch, and a description of each. Filter it with `language`, `gender`, `pitch`, or `q`. Any id it returns works as `voice` or `voice2`; when you also set `language`, use the voice's own language.

**Custom voices**

- Set `voice` to `custom` and pass two recordings of the same adult speaker as https URLs: `voice_audio_url`, 10 to 30 seconds of natural speech, and `voice_consent_audio_url`, the speaker reading "I am the owner of this voice and I consent to Google using this voice to create a synthetic voice model." The statement is accepted in 30 languages; `consent_statements` on that parameter lists each wording.
- Both must be recordings of a real person, in a quiet room on the same microphone. AI-generated audio is not accepted. WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, WEBM and FLAC are accepted, up to 15 MB each.
- The response includes `voice_id` and `voice_id_expires_at`. Pass the `voice_id` as `voice` or `voice2` to reuse the voice for 7 days without new recordings. A `voice_id` works only for the account that created it.
- This model keeps no list of custom voices, so keep the `voice_id` from the response. A custom voice ends when its id expires, so there is nothing to delete.
- In the Playground, set Voice to Custom to use a voice made in the same tab again, or copy its id.

**Delivery direction**

- Put direction for the whole passage in `style_prompt` rather than in the text, for example "warm, unhurried, and reassuring".
- Place vocal tags inline where the sound should happen. Use these English tags even when the text is in another language:

```text
<argh> <breath> <heavy breath> <exhales> <cackle> <cheer> <chuckle> <chuckles> <cough> <cry> <gasp> <giggle> <groan> <growl> <grunt> <grr> <hiss> <laugh> <laughter> <moan> <pant> <pff> <phew> <scream> <shout> <shriek> <sigh> <sighs> <sneeze> <snicker> <snort> <sob> <throat-clearing> <tsk> <whimper> <whispers> <whispering> <yawn> <short pause> <long pause>
```

- Capitalize a word to stress it. Wrap a listener reaction in pipes, for example |mm-hmm|, to add it without starting a new turn.

**Multi-speaker**

- Up to two speakers per request. Start each line with a speaker name and a colon, for example Speaker1: and Speaker2:. The names must match `speaker1_name` and `speaker2_name`.

**Output**

- WAV, MP3, OGG (Opus), ALAW, or MULAW, at 8,000 to 48,000 Hz.
- `POST /v1/audio/speech:stream` sends 16-bit PCM chunks at 24,000 Hz while the audio is generated, then the complete file in the requested format. `speed` is available on `POST /v1/audio/speech` only.

limits.note:
**Limits**

- Text: up to 5,000 characters per request
- Audio billing: 32 output tokens per second of generated audio
- 101 languages. The language of the text is detected automatically.

**Voices**

- The 30 voices in the `voice` list speak every supported language.
- `GET /v1/voices?model=gemini-3-8-flash-lite-tts` lists the full library of more than 2,000 voices across 30 locales, with the language, accent, gender, pitch, and a description of each. Filter it with `language`, `gender`, `pitch`, or `q`. Any id it returns works as `voice` or `voice2`; when you also set `language`, use the voice's own language.

**Custom voices**

- Set `voice` to `custom` and pass two recordings of the same adult speaker as https URLs: `voice_audio_url`, 10 to 30 seconds of natural speech, and `voice_consent_audio_url`, the speaker reading "I am the owner of this voice and I consent to Google using this voice to create a synthetic voice model." The statement is accepted in 30 languages; `consent_statements` on that parameter lists each wording.
- Both must be recordings of a real person, in a quiet room on the same microphone. AI-generated audio is not accepted. WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, WEBM and FLAC are accepted, up to 15 MB each.
- The response includes `voice_id` and `voice_id_expires_at`. Pass the `voice_id` as `voice` or `voice2` to reuse the voice for 7 days without new recordings. A `voice_id` works only for the account that created it.
- This model keeps no list of custom voices, so keep the `voice_id` from the response. A custom voice ends when its id expires, so there is nothing to delete.
- In the Playground, set Voice to Custom to use a voice made in the same tab again, or copy its id.

**Delivery direction**

- Put direction for the whole passage in `style_prompt` rather than in the text, for example "warm, unhurried, and reassuring".
- Place vocal tags inline where the sound should happen. Use these English tags even when the text is in another language:

```text
<argh> <breath> <heavy breath> <exhales> <cackle> <cheer> <chuckle> <chuckles> <cough> <cry> <gasp> <giggle> <groan> <growl> <grunt> <grr> <hiss> <laugh> <laughter> <moan> <pant> <pff> <phew> <scream> <shout> <shriek> <sigh> <sighs> <sneeze> <snicker> <snort> <sob> <throat-clearing> <tsk> <whimper> <whispers> <whispering> <yawn> <short pause> <long pause>
```

- Capitalize a word to stress it. Wrap a listener reaction in pipes, for example |mm-hmm|, to add it without starting a new turn.

**Multi-speaker**

- Up to two speakers per request. Start each line with a speaker name and a colon, for example Speaker1: and Speaker2:. The names must match `speaker1_name` and `speaker2_name`.

**Output**

- WAV, MP3, OGG (Opus), ALAW, or MULAW, at 8,000 to 48,000 Hz.
- `POST /v1/audio/speech:stream` sends 16-bit PCM chunks at 24,000 Hz while the audio is generated, then the complete file in the requested format. `speed` is available on `POST /v1/audio/speech` only.

limits.note:
**Sending audio**

Send a file as multipart `file`, or JSON with `audio_url` or `audio_base64`, in common audio formats. Short clips and long recordings are both accepted.

**Getting the result**

The request returns a `job_id` and a `poll_url` right away. Poll `GET /v1/jobs/<job-id>` until `status` is `completed`. Short clips finish in seconds; long recordings take longer.

**What comes back**

The `result` of the completed job holds the full transcript as `text`, sentence segments with start and end times, and word timestamps. The language is detected automatically, including Chinese dialects.

limits.note:
**Voices**

- 19 voices: 15 English voices and 4 multilingual voices. Emily, Luna, Eric, and Luca have British accents. Abby, Annie, Ava, Beth, Betty, Cally, Cindy, Donna, Andy, Brian, and David have American accents. The multilingual voices `longanhuan_v3.1`, `longanlingxin_v3.1`, `longanfengyue_v3.1`, and `xunanchuan_v3.1` read Chinese, English, and other languages.
- Every voice id ends in `_v3.1`, for example `Emily_v3.1`.

**Custom voices**

- Set `voice` to `custom` and pass `voice_audio_url`, an https URL to 10 to 20 seconds of clear speech from one speaker.
- WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, WEBM and FLAC are accepted, up to 15 MB. Record in a quiet room, without music or other voices.
- The response includes `voice_id` and `voice_id_expires_at`. Pass the `voice_id` as `voice` to reuse the voice for 7 days, on `POST /v1/audio/speech`, `POST /v1/audio/speech:stream` or the realtime socket, where `session.update` takes the same fields and `session.updated` returns the `voice_id`. Only the account that created it can use it.
- Each account can hold 10 custom voices on this model at a time.
- `GET /v1/voices?model=qwen-audio-3-1-tts` lists the model's voices, including your custom voices with their ids. Add `type=custom` to list custom voices alone.
- `DELETE /v1/voices/{voice_id}?model=qwen-audio-3-1-tts` deletes a custom voice, which frees its place at once.
- In the Playground, set Voice to Custom to use a saved voice again, copy its id, or delete it.
- Creating, listing and deleting custom voices adds no charge.

**Delivery direction**

- `instruction` sets emotion, tone, character, pace, and speaking style in natural language, up to 1,000 characters.
- Inline tags inside the text change the delivery from that point, for example `[excited]` or `[whispers]`, or add a one-time sound such as `[laughing]` or `[sighing]`. The full list of tags is on the `input` parameter.
- SSML input is not supported.

**Input limits**

- Up to 10,000 characters per request.
- `language_hints` biases pronunciation for mixed-language text.

**Output**

- MP3, WAV, PCM, or Opus at 8,000 to 48,000 Hz.
- `POST /v1/audio/speech:stream` sends audio chunks while the speech is generated.

**Realtime**

- `WEBSOCKET /v1/realtime?model=qwen-audio-3-1-tts` takes text while it is still being written and returns audio as it is generated. Send `input_text_buffer.append` events, then `input_text_buffer.commit`, or `session.finish` to end the session.
- Audio arrives in `response.audio.delta` events: 16-bit PCM at 24,000 Hz by default, or MP3 or Opus. Set the voice, instruction, format and other options with `session.update`; a change applies from the next segment.
- Text is spoken in segments that end at sentence boundaries, and each segment ends with a `response.done` event carrying its usage.

**Billing**

- Input tokens are the text, and output tokens are the generated audio at 12.5 tokens per second.
- Speed and pitch change the length of the rendered audio but not the billed tokens. An instruction that slows the delivery adds output tokens.

limits.note:
Qwen Image 2.1 combines Pro and Turbo image generation and editing in one model. Pro is selected by default, output starts at 2K, and aspect ratio starts in Auto. Turbo provides a faster, lower-cost option.

**Variants**

- Choose qwen-image-2.1-pro for the highest image quality and complex edits.
- Choose qwen-image-2.1-turbo for faster, lower-cost generation and routine edits.
- Choose with model_variant. Without it, the model id qwen-image-2.1-turbo runs Turbo and every other id of this model runs Pro.

**Modes**

- Text to image from a prompt.
- Image editing and reference-guided generation from one to ten images.
- Direct prompt extension works for generation and editing. Agent prompt extension provides deeper refinement for text-to-image requests only.

**Transparent images**

- Output images are PNG files. For a transparent background, set prompt_extend to false and describe the image in this form: "This is an RGBA image with transparency. A glass perfume bottle. The image has alpha channel and the background is transparent."

**Output limits**

- One to six output images per request.
- 1K, 2K, automatic, aspect-ratio presets, or an exact custom size.
- Exact and custom sizes stay between 512x512 and 2560x2560 pixels in total area, with an aspect ratio from 1:8 to 8:1.

**Billing**

- Each output image is billed at its variant's rate. Reference images are not billed.

**Content safety**

Generated images pass an automated content-safety check. An image flagged as explicit is not returned. Because the image is generated before the check runs, a flagged generation is still billed.

supported_parameters.label: Seed

limits.note:
**What it makes**

- One finished audio file from a written description: narration, dialogue, sound effects, ambience, and music together.
- Describe each voice, the delivery, and the sounds in `input`. There is no voice list.
- Chinese and English.

**Voices from reference clips**

- `references` takes up to 3 clips as URLs or base64 audio data URIs, each up to 30 seconds and 10 MB, in WAV, MP3, or OGG Opus.
- Name them in `input` as `@voice1`, `@voice2`, and `@voice3`, in order, for example: `@voice1 cheerfully says: "What a lovely day."`

**Input limits**

- Up to 3,000 characters per request.
- `instruction` and SSML are not used: all direction goes in `input`.

**Output**

- MP3 (the default), WAV, or PCM at 8,000 to 48,000 Hz, mono or stereo; the defaults are 48,000 Hz and stereo.
- Up to 120 seconds per request, or 240 seconds for a podcast.
- One complete file per request. This model does not stream.

**Billing**

- Input tokens are the description plus each reference clip. Output tokens are the generated audio, about 200 per second.

limits.note:
Text-to-video and image-to-video up to 15 seconds at 1080p, with native synchronized audio. Prompts can run to 5,000 characters, so one prompt can direct performance, camera movement and shot design in detail.

**Modes**

- `t2v`: text to video.
- `i2v`: animate a single image.
- `auto`, the default, uses `i2v` when an image is attached and `t2v` otherwise.

**Output**

- 360p, 540p, 720p and 1080p, 1 to 15 seconds.
- Aspect ratios 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16, 2:3, 3:2 and 21:9 on text-to-video. Image-to-video follows the source image.
- Set `generate_audio_switch` to true for native synchronized audio.
- For several shots in one clip, describe them in order in the prompt, for example "Shot 1: ... Shot 2: ...".

**Billing**

- Billed per second of generated video at the rate for the output resolution, with a higher rate when audio is on.

**Input limits**

- One image: PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 20MB and 10000px on the long edge.
- First and last frame, reference images, video input and clip extension are not available on this model. Use PixVerse V6 for those.

limits.note:
Reads PDFs and images into Markdown, page by page: text in reading order, headings, lists, tables, math, captions, and charts with their data points as a table.

**Input**

- One PDF or image per request: PDF, PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF, BMP, GIF or AVIF, up to 50 MB, as a public URL or a base64 data URI.
- Up to 1,000 pages per request. Choose pages with `pages`, zero-based, as a list such as `[0, 2]` or a string such as `0,2-4`.
- Structured annotation fields are not supported.

**Output**

- Each page as Markdown, with the position of every image region and the page's layout blocks in reading order.
- `include_image_base64` returns each image region as a JPEG data URI.
- `table_format` set to `markdown` or `html` returns each table separately; otherwise tables stay in the Markdown as HTML.
- `extract_header` and `extract_footer` move headers and footers out of the Markdown into their own fields.

**Long documents**

- A request still running after about four and a half minutes returns a job id to poll at `GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}`. Send `Prefer: respond-async` to get it at once.

**Billing**

- Billed per page read, with a minimum of 5 pages per request. A failed request is not billed for pages it did not return.

**Weights**

- FP8.

data.author: alibaba
data.description: Speech synthesis for narration and dubbing, with 4 multilingual voices, plain-language delivery direction, inline emotion tags, and voice cloning.

supported_parameters.name: input
supported_parameters.label: Input
supported_parameters.description: Text to synthesize, up to 10,000 characters per request. These inline tags change the delivery from the point where they appear: [sad], [amazed], [deep and loud shouting], [trembling], [angry], [excited], [sarcastic], [curious], [like dracula], [bored], [tired], [scornful], [shouting], [asmr], [panicked], [mischievously], [empathetic], [whispers], [reluctantly], [crying], [serious], [very slowly], [very fast]. These add a one-time sound at that point: [gasp], [sighing], [clears throat], [giggles], [laughing], [cough], [snorts].

supported_parameters.name: voice
supported_parameters.label: Voice
supported_parameters.description: Voice preset. The 4 voices read Chinese, English, and other languages. Every voice id ends in _v3.1, for example longanlingxin_v3.1. custom clones a voice from voice_audio_url, and the response's voice_id then works here for 7 days. GET /v1/voices lists your custom voices with their ids.

supported_parameters.name: voice_audio_url
supported_parameters.label: Reference audio URL
supported_parameters.description: voice=custom only: an https URL to a 10 to 20 second recording of clear speech from one speaker, the voice to clone (WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, WEBM or FLAC, up to 15 MB). Record it in a quiet room, without music or other voices.

supported_parameters.name: response_format
supported_parameters.label: Response Format
supported_parameters.description: Audio container. mp3 and opus are compressed, wav is uncompressed PCM in a RIFF header, and pcm is headerless raw samples for chunked playback. On the realtime WebSocket the default is pcm and wav is not available.

supported_parameters.name: sample_rate
supported_parameters.label: Sample Rate
supported_parameters.description: Output sample rate in Hz. 24000 suits speech playback, and 48000 gives broadcast-quality output at a larger file size.

supported_parameters.name: speed
supported_parameters.label: Speed
supported_parameters.description: Speaking rate multiplier. 0.5 is half speed and 2.0 is double speed.

supported_parameters.name: pitch
supported_parameters.label: Pitch
supported_parameters.description: Pitch multiplier. Values below 1.0 lower the voice and values above raise it. Pitch also shifts the pace of the rendered audio, so pair it with speed when you want to keep the original duration.

supported_parameters.name: volume
supported_parameters.label: Volume
supported_parameters.description: Output loudness, where 50 is the reference level.

supported_parameters.name: instruction
supported_parameters.label: Instruction
supported_parameters.description: Natural-language direction for delivery, up to 1,000 characters. Controls emotion, tone, character, pace, and speaking style, for example 'Speak quickly in an excited, upbeat tone' or 'Read slowly like a late-night radio host'.

ui.placeholder: Speak quickly in an excited, upbeat tone

supported_parameters.name: language_hints
supported_parameters.label: Language Hints
supported_parameters.description: Language codes that bias pronunciation for mixed-language text, for example ["zh", "en"]. Leave unset to let the model detect the language.

supported_parameters.name: seed
supported_parameters.label: Seed
supported_parameters.description: Sampling seed. Reuse a seed with identical input and settings for a repeatable render.

supported_parameters.name: bit_rate
supported_parameters.label: Bit Rate
supported_parameters.description: Encoder bitrate in bps. Applies to the opus format only, and is ignored for mp3, wav, and pcm.

supported_parameters.name: pronunciation
supported_parameters.label: Pronunciation
supported_parameters.description: Pronunciation overrides keyed by the written form, for example {"重要": "zhong4 yao4"}. Use it to fix names, acronyms, and homographs.

supported_parameters.name: replace
supported_parameters.label: Replace
supported_parameters.description: Literal text substitutions applied before synthesis, for example {"EmpirioLabs": "Empirio Labs"}. Useful for brand names and abbreviations.

supported_parameters.name: enable_markdown_filter
supported_parameters.label: Markdown Filter
supported_parameters.description: Strip Markdown syntax such as asterisks and underscores before synthesis so formatting characters are not read aloud.

limits.note:
**Voices**

- 4 voices that read Chinese, English, and other languages: `longanlingxin_v3.1`, `longanhuan_v3.1`, and `longanfengyue_v3.1` are female, and `xunanchuan_v3.1` is male.
- Every voice id ends in `_v3.1`, for example `longanlingxin_v3.1`.

**Custom voices**

- Set `voice` to `custom` and pass `voice_audio_url`, an https URL to 10 to 20 seconds of clear speech from one speaker.
- WAV, MP3, M4A, OGG, WEBM and FLAC are accepted, up to 15 MB. Record in a quiet room, without music or other voices.
- The response includes `voice_id` and `voice_id_expires_at`. Pass the `voice_id` as `voice` to reuse the voice for 7 days, on `POST /v1/audio/speech`, `POST /v1/audio/speech:stream` or the realtime socket, where `session.update` takes the same fields and `session.updated` returns the `voice_id`. Only the account that created it can use it, on this model only.
- Each account can hold 10 custom voices on this model at a time.
- `GET /v1/voices?model=qwen-audio-3-1-tts-plus` lists the model's voices, including your custom voices with their ids. Add `type=custom` to list custom voices alone.
- `DELETE /v1/voices/{voice_id}?model=qwen-audio-3-1-tts-plus` deletes a custom voice, which frees its place at once.
- In the Playground, set Voice to Custom to use a saved voice again, copy its id, or delete it.
- Creating, listing and deleting custom voices adds no charge.

**Delivery direction**

- `instruction` sets emotion, tone, character, pace, and speaking style in natural language, up to 1,000 characters.
- Inline tags inside the text change the delivery from that point, for example `[excited]` or `[whispers]`, or add a one-time sound such as `[laughing]` or `[sighing]`. The full list of tags is on the `input` parameter.
- SSML input is not supported.

**Input limits**

- Up to 10,000 characters per request.
- `language_hints` biases pronunciation for mixed-language text.

**Output**

- MP3, WAV, PCM, or Opus at 8,000 to 48,000 Hz.
- `POST /v1/audio/speech:stream` sends audio chunks while the speech is generated.

**Realtime**

- `WEBSOCKET /v1/realtime?model=qwen-audio-3-1-tts-plus` takes text while it is still being written and returns audio as it is generated. Send `input_text_buffer.append` events, then `input_text_buffer.commit`, or `session.finish` to end the session.
- Audio arrives in `response.audio.delta` events: 16-bit PCM at 24,000 Hz by default, or MP3 or Opus. Set the voice, instruction, format and other options with `session.update`; a change applies from the next segment.
- Text is spoken in segments that end at sentence boundaries, and each segment ends with a `response.done` event carrying its usage.

**Billing**

- Billed per character of the input text. A Chinese character counts as two characters, and inline tags count as characters. The instruction is not billed.
- On the realtime socket each segment is billed for its own characters.

**Connecting**

Full-duplex voice over a WebSocket at `wss://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1/realtime?model=qwen-audio-3-1-realtime-flash`, authenticated with the ordinary Authorization Bearer header. Configure the session with `session.update` over the socket: voice, instructions, modalities, turn detection, languages and delivery.

**Sending audio**

- Append microphone audio as `input_audio_buffer.append` events.
- Voice activity detection decides when you have stopped speaking, so keep streaming for about a second after the speech ends.

**Language and delivery**

Set `input_language` to the language you speak, which the transcript of your speech is written in, and `output_language` to the language the spoken reply is read in. Each takes auto or one of zh, en, ja, ko, vi, th, id, ar, fr, de, es, pt, ru and it. The output language does not translate the reply, so ask for its language in your instructions too. `speed` (0.5 to 2) sets the speaking rate, `enable_speech_emotion` the expressive delivery, and `max_history_turns` (1 to 50) how many earlier exchanges the model reads.

**Voices**

The voices on this model are its own set. Pick one from the voice list rather than carrying a voice across from another model, or leave it unset and the default is supplied for you.

**Web search**

Web search is off by default. Turn it on with `enable_search`. It works in the same session as function calling, and search results are added to the conversation and count as input tokens.

**Billing**

Audio and text tokens are priced separately in both directions. A spoken reply is billed for its audio output tokens only, and the text output rate applies to replies with no audio. Each completed turn is billed on its own from the usage the model reports.

limits.note:
**Sending audio**

Send a file as multipart `file`, or JSON with `audio_url` or `audio_base64`, in common audio formats. Short clips and long recordings are both accepted.

**Getting the result**

The request returns a `job_id` and a `poll_url` right away. Poll `GET /v1/jobs/<job-id>` until `status` is `completed`. Short clips finish in seconds; long recordings take longer.

**What comes back**

The `result` of the completed job holds the full transcript as `text` and sentence segments with start and end times. The language is detected automatically, including Chinese dialects.

**Billing**

Billed per second of audio, rounded up to the next whole second, at the hourly rate shown.

supported_parameters.name: input_audio_format
supported_parameters.label: Input audio format

supported_parameters.label: Speech threshold
supported_parameters.description: How clear speech must be before it is transcribed, from 0.0 to 1.0. A higher value ignores more background noise and can miss quiet speech. When omitted, the model's own default applies. Also accepted as turn_detection.threshold.

limits.note:
**Connecting**

Live transcription over a WebSocket at `wss://api.empiriolabs.ai/v1/realtime?model=qwen-audio-3-0-asr-stream`, authenticated with the ordinary Authorization Bearer header.

**Sending audio**

Stream 16 kHz mono pcm16 audio with `input_audio_buffer.append`. Voice activity detection decides where each sentence ends, so there is no commit to send.

**Session settings**

Send `session.update` right after `session.created`, before the first audio, with any of these settings: `input_audio_transcription.language` (or the `language` query parameter of the connection URL; `auto` by default), `input_audio_transcription.prompt` with the names and terms the speaker uses (up to 400 characters), `turn_detection.silence_duration_ms` (200 to 6000, default 800) and `turn_detection.threshold` (0.0 to 1.0), and `input_audio_noise_reduction` (`near_field` or `far_field`). `keep_dialect` keeps Chinese dialect words as spoken. A setting changed while audio is streaming ends the sentence in progress and applies to the audio sent after it.

**What comes back**

`conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.delta` events carry the sentence so far while the speaker is still talking, and `conversation.item.input_audio_transcription.completed` carries the settled sentence at each pause.

**Billing**

Billed per second of the audio you stream, silence included, at the hourly rate shown. The session is billed when it ends.

limits.note:
Generates 3 to 30 second clips at 24 fps in 720p or 1080p, each with a native stereo audio track.

**Inputs**

- Text to video: prompt only.
- Keyframes: a first frame (`image`), middle frames (`middle_images`) and a last frame (`image_end`). The video follows the first frame's aspect ratio.
- Reference images (`reference_images`): characters, objects, scenes or style to use.
- Reference videos (`reference_videos`): motion, camera work or style to follow, 3 to 30 seconds each.
- Video edit (`video`): a video to edit, 3 to 30 seconds. The result keeps its length and aspect ratio.
- Up to 10 images and 5 videos per request. In the prompt, refer to images as @image_1, @image_2 (first frame, middle frames, last frame, then references) and to videos as @video_1, @video_2 (the video to edit first).

**In the Playground**

One attached image is the first frame, two are the first and last frames, and three or more are references. The first attached video is the one edited; any others are references.

**Media limits**

- Images: JPG or PNG, at least 300 px, aspect ratio between 2:5 and 5:2, up to 30 MB.
- Videos: MP4 or MOV, 3 to 30 seconds, 700 to 4553 px per side, up to 300 MB.

**Billing**

- Without a video input: billed per second of the generated clip at the resolution you request.
- With a video input (a video to edit or a reference video): billed at the video input rate on twice the length of the generated clip, or on the input plus the output when the input is longer.

**Billing**

- Without a video input: billed per second of the generated clip.
- With a video input (a video to edit or a reference video): billed at the video input rate on twice the length of the generated clip, or on the input plus the output when the input is longer.
